faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for a 14-year-old in Australia?
faqs.a: There is no single national rate for 14-year-olds. The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) applies to adult employees. For juniors under 16, award rates or registered agreements set a percentage of the adult rate, often around 40–50% depending on the industry. Check the relevant award or the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific job.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the adult minimum wage of $26.44, annual gross is about $52,289. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: Does superannuation apply to junior employees?
faqs.a: Yes, super guarantee (currently 12% of ordinary earnings) applies to most employees, including juniors, if they earn $450 or more before tax in a calendar month. Super is paid on top of your hourly rate, not deducted from it. The contribution is capped at the maximum super contribution base ($270,830 for 2026–27).

## Understanding the Minimum Wage Australia 14-Year-Old

If you’re a 14-year-old starting your first job, you’re likely curious about the **minimum wage australia 14-year-old** and how it translates into weekly, fortnightly, or annual pay. In Australia, the National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission, but junior employees often receive a percentage of that rate under an award or agreement. This guide explains how to convert your hourly rate to annual figures, the role of superannuation, and what to expect for tax.

### The National Minimum Wage and Junior Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for adult employees working a 38-hour week. This equates to $1,004.90 per week. However, for a 14-year-old, the rate is typically lower. Most awards set junior pay as a proportion of the adult rate—for example, 40% to 50% for under-16s. The exact percentage depends on your industry and award. Always check your specific award or the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) for the correct rate. The **minimum wage australia 14-year-old** is not a single figure; it varies by job type.

### Converting Hourly Pay to Annual, Fortnightly, and Weekly

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38-hour week unless your contract states otherwise. For example, if you earn $26.44 per hour (adult rate), your annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,289.44. For a junior rate of, say, $13.22 per hour (50% of adult), annual gross would be $13.22 × 38 × 52 = $26,144.72.

To find your **fortnightly** pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Weekly pay is hourly rate × hours per week. So at $26.44/hour for 38 hours, weekly = $1,004.72, fortnightly = $2,009.44. This helps when budgeting for bills or savings.

Remember: this calculation assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It’s a simple estimate. For a more precise tool, use [the timesheet](/) on our site.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you’re a casual employee, you’re entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. For the adult minimum wage, that’s $33.05 per hour. For a 14-year-old, the loading applies to the junior base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into our calculator—use the base rate and tick the casual checkbox.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% (from 1 July 2026) of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross is $26,144.72, your employer adds $3,137.37 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it’s extra.

### Tax on Your Earnings

As a resident for tax purposes, you pay no tax on the first $18,200 of income (2026–27 rates). From $18,201 to $45,000, the rate is 15%. Most 14-year-olds earning below $18,200 will pay zero tax, but you may still need to lodge a return if tax was withheld. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, but low-income earners may be exempt. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed estimate.

### Comparing Your Pay to Averages

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). This is an average, not a median, and includes all adult full-time workers. For all employees (including part-time), total earnings average $1,579.20 per week. These figures are much higher than what a 14-year-old typically earns, reflecting seniority and experience. Your pay as a junior is not a job median; it’s an entry-level rate under an award.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award. Most 14-year-olds will be covered by an industry award (e.g., retail, hospitality, fast food). Award rates for juniors are often higher than the National Minimum Wage percentage because they include specific junior percentages. Always check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [reference tables](/data) or [pay guides](/blog). The **minimum wage australia 14-year-old** in your award may be different from the national figure.

### Using Our Hourly Conversion Tool

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page helps you switch between hourly, weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and select your hours per week. The tool uses the 38-hour default but you can adjust it. For casuals, tick the 25% loading box. The result shows gross annual, super estimate, and tax using the 2026–27 resident scale. Remember, this is an estimate—not a determination of your actual pay.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting. For a junior at $13.22/hour for 38 hours, fortnightly gross = $13.22 × 38 × 2 = $1,004.72. After tax (if any) and Medicare, your take-home will be lower. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide to estimate net pay.

### Key Takeaways

- The **minimum wage australia 14-year-old** is not a single rate; check your award.
- Annual gross = hourly × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours unless otherwise).
- Fortnightly = weekly × 2.
- Super (12%) is paid on top of your hourly rate.
- Casual loading (25%) is added to the base rate.
- Tax-free threshold up to $18,200; Medicare levy applies.
- ABS averages are for adults; your pay as a junior is not a median.

For more details, explore our [about the timesheet](/about) page or the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) topic. Always consult the Fair Work Ombudsman for your exact entitlements.
